transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/time: 2026-07-11 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood AE), Sasha Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Rivera (Redwood SE); Rita Gomez (VP Eng, Tidewell), Dulce Ortega (Cloud Architect), Markus Hsu (Security Lead), Ben Park (Network Eng)

Auto-generated Summary (may be imperfect):
Tidewell is exploring Redwood Private for inference hosting behind their VPCs in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Main constraints: strict egress allow-listing, EU data residency for some PII processing, integration with customer KMS (AWS KMS, possible HSM), and desire for a deterministic pilot with single VPC peering + NAT IP slices. They asked about failover to Hosted, latency profile, and audit logs.

00:00 Liam Chen: "All right, thanks everyone for joining. quick intros — I'm Liam, AE on Redwood, Sasha and Noah are our solutions folks — could you go around and say names and roles on the Tidewell side?"
00:10 Rita Gomez: "Hi, Rita here — VP of Engineering, overseeing MLOps and infra work. We're evaluating private options for LLM inference, mainly because of egress and residency rules."
00:20 Dulce Ortega: "Hi, Dulce, Cloud Architect — I'll be the primary network contact; I'll share peering topology and Transit GW details later."
00:28 Markus Hsu: "Markus, Security — SOC2, KMS stuff, audit logs are my lane."
00:34 Ben Park: "Ben, networking — NAT, IP planning, routing, all that."
00:40 Sasha Patel: "Great, thanks. quick overview: Redwood Private gives you a customer-managed dataplane, you can run inference in your VPCs or via private endpoints. We'll go through connectivity options — peering, privatelink, transit — and egress patterns. Any high level goals we should be aware of?"
00:52 Rita Gomez: "We need to keep production inference in our VPCs for now. Some models can live in Hosted but the health app workflow that touches EU PII must stay inside eu-west-1. So we need a clear playbook for region gating and egress IPs. Also cost and latency — we need 90th p95 under 150ms for our 1k token flows if possible." 
01:10 Noah Rivera: "Okay, p95 150ms is reasonable depending on model choice and batching. We'll map model variants. question on connectivity: do you have a Transit Gateway today or are you doing VPC peering?"
01:18 Dulce Ortega: "We use a Transit Gateway in AWS for our app VPCs. For the initial pilot we prefer peering from a dedicated inference VPC to our app VPC via TGW attachments — simpler for routing tables. We also need to know whether Redwood needs incoming connectivity or we call outbound to Redwood endpoints via PrivateLink."
01:36 Sasha Patel: "So two main patterns: 1) attach Redwood nodes directly into your VPC as managed private nodes — then routing stays internal and egress is yours; 2) use PrivateLink/private endpoints where you keep nodes in Redwood-managed infra but traffic never traverses internet — it's routed via interface endpoints. Both have tradeoffs. For deterministic egress IPs and full network control the attach-in-VPC pattern gives you the most control."
01:58 Ben Park: "Attach-in-VPC sounds better for us if we can provide subnets and security groups. But then how do you handle scaling and GPU scheduling? We don't want to be babysitting nodes."
02:10 Sasha Patel: "Redwood's private package supports a customer-managed dataplane where our control plane coordinates jobs but the inference runtime runs in your subnets. We provide a deployment manifest. Autoscaling can use your cluster autoscaler or our agent can request new instances — we recommend a dedicated pool and an autoscale policy file. We'll share example deployment yaml. The runtime handles KV cache and prefix caching locally — reduces cross-AZ traffic."
02:34 Rita Gomez: "On the security side, Markus — we need keys to stay in our KMS, and for some models we need HSM-backed keys. can Redwood integrate with external KMS?"
02:44 Markus Hsu: "Also need to confirm log collection: request/response audit logs, model versioning logs, and the ability to forward logs to our Splunk/S3 with encryption at rest."
02:54 Noah Rivera: "Yes, we integrate with customer KMS for envelope encryption. For HSM, we support KMS-backed HSM providers (bring-your-own) — we have a validated integration path but we'll need a runbook and possibly an attestation. For logs, private deployments can push telemetry to your logging endpoints or you can export from the private control plane; we can support a forwarder to S3 or a syslog endpoint."
03:16 Ben Park: "Egress IPs: we have a strict allow-list for external APIs. if Redwood nodes make outbound calls (for model downloads or registry), what IPs will we need to approve? can you provide a static set?"
03:28 Sasha Patel: "If you attach in-VPC, egress is your NAT — you control the IPs. If you use PrivateLink to our infra, we can provide a small set of stable egress IPs per region (we publish them in the private deployment docs). There's also an option to bring a NAT IP pool and we can coordinate to use your egress paths. We'll put this in the network diagram."
03:50 Rita Gomez: "Great. For EU models that touch PII, we need data residency and no cross-border replication. So we want explicit isolation: inference for EU workloads must run in eu-west-1 VPCs only, and backups/metrics must not go out of region. is that supported?"
04:05 Noah Rivera: "Yes, you can pin model versions and route requests by region or by tenant. Our rollout/routing policies can enforce region-local execution. Metric retention can be configured — we can keep telemetry locally and forward aggregated metrics only. We'll need to map your tenants to routing rules."
04:20 Markus Hsu: "On compliance, we need SOC2 attestation, and an architectural diagram for auditors showing where keys live, log flow, and who has access. Also SSO — we want SAML with SCIM provisioning for RBAC."
04:34 Sasha Patel: "We have SOC2 Type II docs and can share a SOC2 pack; SAML + SCIM is supported for the console and admin RBAC. For the private control plane, we can configure role mappings. We'll share sample RBAC mappings."
04:45 Ben Park: "One more network question — how do you handle egress for model downloads and frequent model updates? We can't allow large bursts from outside — we need to plan bandwidth."
04:58 Liam Chen: "Good point. For the pilot we recommend pre-fetching model artifacts into your VPC or a local S3 mirror. Redwood's model distributor can use signed URLs and you can serve from an internal S3 endpoint. That avoids heavy egress. We'll share the artifact sync pattern."
05:15 Rita Gomez: "Pilot scope? we were thinking 2 apps, 1 EU tenant, 1 US tenant, small concurrency to validate latency and egress playbook."
05:24 Sasha Patel: "Sounds good. Proposal: 2 inference nodes in each region attached to your VPC, 1 small gpu per node, synthetic load + a sampling of real prompts (we'll redact). We'll test failover: if capacity in eu-west-1 is saturated, the request must not cross the border — we should ensure strict routing and return 429 or fallback to smaller model in-region. We'll document behavior."
05:50 Dulce Ortega: "Can you run a dry-run where your control plane is still in Redwood but nodes are in our VPC so we can see traffic patterns?"
05:58 Noah Rivera: "Yes, that's the standard private onboarding flow — control plane out of band, runtime in your VPC. For ultimate isolation we also have a fully air-gapped option but that has a longer lead time."
06:10 Markus Hsu: "Regarding keys, can you supply logs that show key usage per-request? Auditors want to see cryptographic operations audited."
06:18 Sasha Patel: "We can emit key-use events and forward them to your audit sink. We'll map the event schema in the runbook."
06:26 Ben Park: "Operational note: we'll need a CIDR planning doc. we prefer /22 for the pilot subnets and will provide route table entries. we also want low blast radius for IPs."
06:36 Liam Chen: "Understood. We'll send a network diagram template and a step-by-step onboarding checklist. I'll include recommended subnet sizes and security group examples."
06:45 Rita Gomez: "Pricing / cost question: if we run nodes in our VPC, is the pricing purely software/service fee or do we pay for the nodes?"
06:54 Liam Chen: "For private-in-VPC, the model is split: you provide infra spend (instances) and Redwood charges a software/service fee for the runtime, telemetry, and control plane usage. For Dedicated vs Private we can show comparative TCO. We'll include a sample cost model in the follow-up."
07:09 Dulce Ortega: "Latency: we will need to instrument from our app to the inference endpoint and make sure DNS resolution and ENIs don't add unexpected jitter."
07:18 Noah Rivera: "We'll provide a tracing hook and a small test harness. Also, prefix/KV cache reduces token latency for repeated prompts; we'll recommend cache warms before each run."
07:30 Rita Gomez: "Okay, next steps recap?"
07:33 Liam Chen: "Recap: Redwood to send network diagram, NAT/egress options, SOC2 + KMS runbook, RBAC samples, and a pilot proposal with cost. Tidewell to send CIDR blocks, TGW topology, and regulatory constraints. We'll aim to have the pilot kickoff next week pending exchange of docs. Any blockers?"
07:52 Markus Hsu: "No blockers; just need the KMS integration docs asap for procurement review."
07:58 Dulce Ortega: "I'll compile CIDRs and route tables and send by end of week."
08:03 Ben Park: "I'll be available to review the subnet sizing and NAT plan."
